Source and verification code for the paper *Subexponential Weighted Counting and Exact Optimisation* by Deep Bhattacharjee.

The paper reproduces, with credit, the summation routine of OpenAI's preprint "The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False" (25 October 2026) for sparse formulas, and proves from it, with complete proofs, that the following are computed deterministically in time 2^{o(n)}: the whole weight profile of a sparse weighted constraint system (Max-k-SAT, Min-k-SAT, the count of optimal assignments), the number of satisfying assignments of each Hamming weight, Max-Cut and the maximum and minimum bisection of a sparse graph, the weighted independence polynomial of every graph (hence the independence and clique numbers and their counts), knapsack with an arbitrary conflict graph and several capacities, Vertex Cover in time 2^{o(k)} + poly(n), partition functions and homomorphism counts on bounded-degree graphs, the density of states of Ising and Potts systems with polynomially bounded couplings, dominating sets, matchings, hitting sets and sparse permanents, counting under a congruence, several linear statistics at once, Max-q-Cut and balanced partitions, f-factors, orientations, edge colourings and nowhere-zero flows on bounded-degree graphs, the Tutte polynomial on every hyperbola (x-1)(y-1) = q with q a positive integer, the weight enumerator, minimum distance and maximum-likelihood decoding of codes with sparse parity checks, bounded-degree hypergraphs, linear-size circuits, 0-1 and bounded integer programs with sparse rows (exact cover with bounded frequency, partially ordered knapsack), Max-Cut, Ising ground states, Max-k-SAT and sparse integer programs at every average degree o(sqrt(log n / log log n)), Max-Cut on dense graphs that differ in few pairs from a graph of bounded rank, such as a blow-up of a graph on o(n/log n) vertices, k-SAT in SE and SNP ⊆ SE.

Version 1.4.0 extends the dense results. If the weights of a graph are a quadratic form in s vertex weights, the cut depends only on the values of those weights on one side, and these are linear statistics; with a sparse perturbation on top, the cut profile is computed in time 2^{o(n)} whenever s log(nΩ) = o(n) and the perturbation has o(n sqrt(log n / log log n)) pairs (Theorem 7.23). This covers every graph that differs in that many pairs from a blow-up of a graph on o(n/log n) vertices, complete multipartite graphs among them (Corollary 7.24), and contains Corollary 7.22. A count shows that these classes contain almost no graphs and not G(n,1/2) (Remark 7.25): Max-Cut on every graph in time 2^{o(n)} is not proved. code/check_density.py now runs 8 checks.

Files: `subexponential-weighted-counting.pdf` (the paper), `subexponential-weighted-counting-tex.zip` (LaTeX source and figures), `subexponential-weighted-counting-arxiv.tar.gz` (arXiv-style source). The exact-arithmetic check program and its recorded output are in `code/`.
